summary: A BMW sedan made a prohibited left turn and hit a driverless Cruise autonomous vehicle in San Francisco, damaging its bumper. The BMW driver left the scene and no one was injured.
technical_summary: A Cruise vehicle operating in driverless mode entered an intersection on a green light when another car made an illegal left turn from the adjacent lane without signaling. The autonomous vehicle braked but could not avoid contact. The report attributes the collision to the other driver.

summary: On May 6, 2010, US stock indices plunged and rebounded within minutes. Authorities later alleged that a trader using a modified automated trading program to place and cancel large fake orders helped trigger the crash.
technical_summary: A trader modified commercially available trading software to automatically place and rapidly cancel large sell orders in index futures (spoofing), creating order imbalances that contributed to the market collapse. Regulators were criticized for failing to detect the activity for years.

notes: AIID lists Barclays Capital and Waddell & Reed, but the excerpts attribute the event to an individual trader's spoofing software; developer and deployer left empty. Causation was debated.

summary: Several US police departments dropped ShotSpotter gunshot detection after finding it unreliable and costly. Officials reported missed shots, false alarms, few arrests and high spending relative to results.
technical_summary: ShotSpotter uses networks of acoustic sensors and software to detect and locate gunfire. Departments reported accuracy around 50 percent, missed gunfire, false alerts, and little effect on crime, with high licensing and overtime costs, leading them to discontinue the system.

summary: Malaysian courts in Sabah and Sarawak piloted an AI tool that recommended sentences, including in drug possession cases. A defense lawyer objected, saying the recommended sentence was too harsh and the tool lacked legal basis and consultation.
technical_summary: A state-built system analyzed a database of 2014-2019 cases and, using inputs such as the charge, age, employment and socio-economic data, recommended sentences to magistrates. Critics raised concerns about bias, lack of legal provision, absent consultation and over-influence on judges.

lifecycle_stage.quote: courts in Sabah and neighbouring Sarawak were testing the AI tool for sentencing recommendations as part of a nationwide pilot

notes: The harshness of the sentence is the defense lawyer's claim; judges make the final decision.

summary: Scammers in China bypassed WeChat Pay's face verification by turning victims' selfies from social media into animated GIFs that mimicked blinking and head turns, then stole money from accounts. Police arrested three suspects.
technical_summary: WeChat Pay's facial recognition liveness check asks users to blink or turn their heads. Fraudsters took selfies from victims' WeChat Moments and converted them into GIFs performing those actions, fooling the verification and enabling transfers after account access was obtained.

summary: A finance worker at a multinational firm in Hong Kong paid out about $25 million after a video call in which fraudsters used deepfakes to impersonate the company's chief financial officer and colleagues, according to police.
technical_summary: Scammers built deepfake video and cloned voices of executives and staff from publicly available footage, then staged a multi-person video conference and follow-up messages to pressure an employee into 15 transfers to local bank accounts. The fraud was discovered only after contacting head office.

summary: A sidewalk delivery robot in Los Angeles rolled through police caution tape at a crime scene, and the video went viral. The company said a remote human operator, not the robot's software, chose to proceed.
technical_summary: A Level 4 autonomy delivery robot paused at yellow tape; after bystanders lifted the tape, a remote human operator who had taken control at the intersection decided to proceed. The company called it a human judgment error and began developing new protocols for operator and AI.

summary: California Highway Patrol officers found a man asleep at the wheel of a Tesla Model S driving at about 70 mph on Highway 101 and stopped it by slowing in front of the car, which appeared to be on Autopilot. The driver was arrested on suspicion of drunk driving.

Officers braked in front of it so the driver-assist system slowed the car to a stop. Autopilot use was not confirmed, and the case raised questions about preventing driver abuse.

summary: The National Eating Disorders Association took its chatbot Tessa offline after it gave users weight-loss and calorie-tracking advice, which experts said can be harmful to people with eating disorders. The group said it had not authorized the AI upgrade.

summary: Researchers found that image-generation models iGPT and SimCLR, trained on unlabeled internet images, learned racial and gender stereotypes, such as completing cropped photos of women in revealing clothing.
technical_summary: Unsupervised models that learn pixel embeddings from internet images absorb the biases of the data, which overrepresents scantily clad women and harmful stereotypes. Researchers adapted an implicit-association test to measure these learned associations without human labels.

sector.quote: The latest paper demonstrates an even deeper source of toxicity

failure_mode.quote: the internet has an overrepresentation of scantily clad women and other often harmful stereotypes

affected_population.quote: the internet has an overrepresentation of scantily clad women and other often harmful stereotypes

notes: Research finding about research models; no deployed-product harm is described in the excerpt.
